<style>
/* ===================================================================
   Spokane ENT / Columbia Surgical Specialists — global UI skin
   ONE source of truth for the tree's look & feel. Lives in script_code;
   a one-line script adds class `cse-skin` to <body> so every rule is
   scoped to this tree only. Edit here -> re-import to update everywhere.
   =================================================================== */
:root{
  --cse-ink:#2D3748; --cse-mut:#64748B;
  --cse-navy:#1F3A54; --cse-navy-dk:#16283B; --cse-teal:#3F8F6B; --cse-teal-tint:#E3F1EC; --cse-teal-bd:#BEDDD0;
  --cse-surface:#FFFFFF; --cse-soft:#F4F6F8; --cse-bd:#E2E8F0;
  --cse-red:#C0362C; --cse-red-bg:#FCECEA; --cse-red-bd:#F2C6C1;
  --cse-amber:#92620A; --cse-amber-bg:#FDF3E0; --cse-amber-bd:#F0DBA6;
  --cse-radius:10px;
  --cse-font:-apple-system,BlinkMacSystemFont,"Segoe UI",Roboto,Helvetica,Arial,sans-serif;
}
body.cse-skin{ font-family:var(--cse-font); color:var(--cse-ink); line-height:1.55; }
.cse-skin p, .cse-skin li{ font-size:16px; }
.cse-skin p:empty{ display:none; }

/* de-noise: crush old pasted inline styling back to the uniform base */
.cse-skin [style*="color: rgb(255, 0, 0)"], .cse-skin [style*="color:rgb(255,0,0)"],
.cse-skin [style*="font-size: 24px"], .cse-skin [style*="font-size:24px"]{
  color:inherit !important; font-size:inherit !important;
}

/* native answer buttons (primary/secondary already set via css_include;
   these are a fallback so styling stays consistent if class names match) */
.cse-skin .btn, .cse-skin .zt-button, .cse-skin .answer-button{
  font-family:var(--cse-font) !important; border-radius:8px !important; font-weight:600 !important;
}

/* ---- alert / outcome card (used by triage & scheduling-note nodes) ---- */
.cse-skin .cse-card{ border:1px solid var(--cse-bd); border-radius:var(--cse-radius); overflow:hidden; background:var(--cse-surface); margin:4px 0 16px; }
.cse-skin .cse-card-head{ display:flex; align-items:center; gap:10px; padding:14px 18px; border-bottom:1px solid var(--cse-bd); }
.cse-skin .cse-card-title{ font-size:16px; font-weight:700; letter-spacing:.02em; text-transform:uppercase; }
.cse-skin .cse-card-body{ padding:16px 18px; }
.cse-skin .cse-card-body p{ margin:0 0 10px; } .cse-skin .cse-card-body p:last-child{ margin-bottom:0; }
.cse-skin .cse-card-icon{ font-size:20px; line-height:1; }

.cse-skin .cse-card--danger .cse-card-head{ background:var(--cse-red-bg); border-color:var(--cse-red-bd); }
.cse-skin .cse-card--danger .cse-card-title,.cse-skin .cse-card--danger .cse-card-icon{ color:var(--cse-red); }
.cse-skin .cse-card--caution .cse-card-head{ background:var(--cse-amber-bg); border-color:var(--cse-amber-bd); }
.cse-skin .cse-card--caution .cse-card-title,.cse-skin .cse-card--caution .cse-card-icon{ color:var(--cse-amber); }
.cse-skin .cse-card--neutral .cse-card-head{ background:var(--cse-soft); }
.cse-skin .cse-card--neutral .cse-card-title,.cse-skin .cse-card--neutral .cse-card-icon{ color:var(--cse-navy); }
</style>
<script>
(function(){
  function applySkin(){
    if(document.body && !document.body.classList.contains('cse-skin')){
      document.body.classList.add('cse-skin');
    }
  }
  applySkin();
  if(document.readyState === 'loading'){
    document.addEventListener('DOMContentLoaded', applySkin);
  }
})();
</script>

A by-name referral is when the SENT doctor's name is used in the clinical note, is handwritten on the face sheet, typed in the "comments" section or in the "to provider" field, or when a patient requests a specific SENT doctor.

For these referrals, triage the symptom and book with the doctor if listed.  if not, book with a listed doctor and notify the requested doctor.

Some patients are referred from another ENT practice, by-name to a specific doctor at SENT.  In those circumstances, click "back" and follow the "Referred by an ENT practice" pathway, keeping in mind that scheduling should occur with the named doctor at SENT.

If booking with Schmitt/Babajanian/Stoddard/Cruz/Dunham/Olds, send an inbasket notification after scheduling the appointment.  Also inform the patient that the appointment date will be reviewed and possibly expedited.

126.content:
🕑Wax Reminder

Ask the patient if they have ANY ear symptoms - hearing loss, pain, discharge, plugged sensation, etc.  If so, press the "back" button and follow that pathway.  As for all non-wax ear issues, an audiogram should be scheduled with the appointment.

If the patient truly describes otherwise asymptomatic wax, of if the only goal of the appointment is removal of wax that could not be removed elsewhere, then schedule without an audiogram by clicking the red button below.

The "first line" providers for wax are Karee Ledeboer and Robert Dieter.  Schedule with another provider only if substantially earlier availability is identified.

Click the following button to continue.

203.content: # claude.md — ent scheduling (tree 730082745) ## Purpose Internal staff-facing triage/scheduling tool for **Spokane ENT** (a practice under **Columbia Surgical Specialists**, Spokane WA). A scheduler/nurse walks a caller through their ENT symptom(s) and the tree routes to the correct provider group / urgency tier / scheduling instruction. Not patient-facing; no external system integrations (no CX Actions) by design — confirmed with the account owner (Aksana), Sep 2026. ## Architecture - Root (node 160): "Have you been seen at Spokane ENT before?" -> node 1 "Chief Complaint" (Ear/Nose/Throat/Other) -> symptom-specific branches -> either a direct outcome/provider-group node, or into node 77 "Physician Triage" (a 17-option master routing list) for complex/ambiguous cases. - **Ear and Nose are now script-driven (Sep 2026 consolidation pass)** — see "Script-driven branches" below. Throat, Other, and the Established Patient cluster are still pure branching `Content` chains (unchanged, not yet converted — see Changelog for why). - Terminal nodes are either a **provider/routing group** (e.g. "Complex Sinus Group", "Straightforward Ear Group") or a **scope-exclusion notice** ("Spokane ENT does not manage X"). These, and the alert/instructional interstitials in front of some of them, are untouched by the Ear/Nose consolidation — the new script-driven branches route straight into the same nodes the old question chains used to land on. - Alert/reminder screens (`cse-card` component, see Conventions) sit as single-button interstitials before certain outcomes — staff must read a clinical note before continuing. ## Script-driven branches (Ear, Nose, Other) — Sep 2026 Both follow the same three-node shape: **intake (Content, native fields) -> eval script -> router (Scoring)**. - **Ear** — node 2 "Ear Symptoms & Details" (native `select`/`number` fields, each follow-up gated by `config.conditional` on the prior answer) -> node 6 "Compute Ear Triage Entry Node" (Script, sets `ear_entry_node`) -> node 13 "Route Ear Triage" (Scoring, one button per distinct `ear_entry_node` value, `op:"def"` fallback -> 56). Replaces the original 15-node question chain (2,6,13,15,17,68,82,87,97,99,102,122,123,134,146 — all pure Q&A nodes with no outcome content of their own, confirmed by a full inbound-edge audit before deletion). - **Nose** — node 3 "Nose Symptoms & Details" -> node 15 "Compute Nose Triage Entry Node" (Script, sets `nose_entry_node`) -> node 17 "Route Nose Triage" (Scoring, `op:"def"` fallback -> 61). Replaces the original 9-node question chain (3,27,32,39,96,100,101,103,177). - Node 1's existing "Ear" -> 2 and "Nose" -> 3 buttons needed **no changes** — the new intake nodes were deliberately given the old chain-head ids (house numbering rule: reuse the lowest freed ids after a deletion). - **Vestigial branches found and folded in** (both answers of the original question always led to the same place — a real latent inefficiency in the pre-2026-09 tree, independent of this consolidation): node 6 "Otorrhea, Hearing Loss?" (reached from Pain, age>=18) — both answers -> 56, so "Pain" now routes straight to 56 regardless of age; node 39 "Nasal Trauma?" — both answers -> 61; node 27's entire "Associated Sinonasal Symptoms?" sub-tree (27->103->61 and 27->96->61) — every path out of it lands on 61 regardless of the answers given, so "Facial Pressure/Pain" now routes straight to 61. - **Numeric age fields replace discrete age-bracket buttons** (e.g. original buttons "<18" / ">18 but <65" / ">65"). The new `ear_age`/`ear_candidate_age`/`nose_age` number fields use the boundary convention `age >= 65` and `age >= 18` (i.e. an exact 18 or 65 falls into the older bucket) — the original discrete buttons left the exact boundary to staff judgment, so this is a defined interpretation, not a re-validated clinical rule.
